index.hero_h1:
Private internet,
no account, no logs.
index.hero_lede: One tap connects you through independent Flux nodes in dozens of countries. Free at 100 KB/s forever. Full speed for $0.99/month paid in FLUX straight from your wallet, or $1.99 by card. No email, no account, no company that can hand over what it never had.
index.how_h2: No accounts. No server of ours. Just the chain.
index.how_lede:
Your WireGuard key is your identity. Payment is a fact on the Flux blockchain that every
        gateway reads independently. If our company vanished tomorrow, the deployed gateways keep running.
index.step1_p:
The app makes a WireGuard keypair on your device and enrolls it at the nearest
          gateway. Free tier is throttled to 100 KB/s server-side — connected in seconds, no signup.
index.step2_p:
Send %PRICE_FLUX% FLUX ($0.99/month) to the payment address with your key's code in the transaction
          message. One tap opens your wallet with it pre-filled.
index.step3_p:
Every gateway scans the chain and flips your key to full speed within ~1 minute — on all
          servers at once, for 30 days. No activation, no login. Prepay to stack months.
index.pricing_h2: Free that actually works. Cheap when you need more.
index.pricing_lede:
The free tier is funded by subscribers and capped so it can't be abused — genuinely usable
        for browsing and messaging. Full speed is one wallet transfer away.
index.free_li3: No logs, no email, no signup
index.prem_li1: Full speed — up to 50 Mbit/s per connection
index.prem_li2: Unlocks on all gateways at once
index.prem_li3: Pay from any FLUX wallet, prepay months
index.prem_li4: Still no account — no logs, no email, nothing stored
index.apps_h2: One connect button, on every screen you own.
index.apps_lede:
The same beautiful client on web and mobile, with desktop coming soon — one design language on
        every screen. Pay on the web with your phone's Device code and it unlocks automatically over the chain within a minute.
index.app_web_p:
Generates your key in the browser and gives you a WireGuard config + QR to import into the
          WireGuard app. Also hosts the pay-in-FLUX upgrade page. No install to set up or pay.
index.app_desktop_p:
A calm menu-bar app for macOS, Windows and Linux. Kill switch, auto-reconnect and gateway
          failover run quietly in the tray. Signed ~10 MB installers.
index.app_mobile_p: iOS and Android, store-compliant. Upgrade on the web — or in the app, where it offers a subscription — and your phone flips to full speed on its own. Premium rides on your key, not on an account, so there is no lock-in.
index.trust_h2: We can't hand over what we never had.
index.trust_lede:
Most VPNs ask you to trust a no-logs promise. CumulusVPN removes the thing you'd have to
        trust: there's no account to log, no database of users, and no central server that owns the fleet.
index.trust1_p:
Gateways enforce tier per key and route traffic — nothing about who or what you browse is
          stored. DNS runs through the tunnel, and the gateway sends it on encrypted (DNS over HTTPS) to Cloudflare or the resolver you choose, which sees the gateway's address, never yours.
index.trust2_p: No email, no password, no account. Your WireGuard key is your only identity, and premium is unlocked on the blockchain against a hash of it — not against you. If you pay by card, Stripe holds those details; we never see them.
index.trust3_p:
The apps and the gateway are public. Read the code, build it yourself, or run your own —
          the payment and entitlement protocol is fully documented.
index.trust4_p:
Exits run as apps on Flux nodes with static IPs, operated by independent third parties — never on
          other users' devices, so not a residential botnet. Over 6,500 nodes across the network.
index.trust5_p:
Clients discover live gateways from the Flux network itself, with a signed bundled
          fallback. No single point to seize, block, or switch off.
index.trust6_p:
Modern, audited, fast. You never touch a config file — the app handles keys, tunnels and
          failover. WireGuard is the wire; the experience is one button.
index.band_p: Start free in seconds — no email, no account. Upgrade whenever you want full speed, and paid in FLUX your $0.99 literally buys the network's own compute.

support.intro_p: No account needed — most answers are right here. There's no login and no password to forget — just a recovery key to keep safe. Still stuck? Email us.
support.a1:
A decentralized WireGuard VPN that runs on the Flux cloud. One tap routes
          your traffic through independent Flux nodes worldwide. No account, no logs.
support.a2:
No. On first launch the app generates a WireGuard key on your device —
          that key is your only identity. No email, password, or phone number, ever.
support.a3:
Open the app, pick a country, and tap connect. On the first connection your
          phone shows a standard operating-system VPN-permission prompt — approve it once.
support.q4: Is the free tier really free?
support.a4: Yes, forever. It's capped at 100 KB/s (fine for browsing and chat), with no payment details and no trial.
support.a5:
Every gateway in the fleet — 30+ countries at launch — and the list updates
          live from the network.
support.a6: No activity logs. Gateways hold minimal routing state in RAM only, erased on disconnect or restart. Your browsing, DNS queries, and traffic are never recorded. See the privacy policy for the full detail.
support.a7:
A WireGuard keypair generated on your device. The private key is never sent to
          us or to a gateway; only the public key is shared, to route your tunnel. It's a pseudonym, not tied
          to your identity. The phone app keeps an encrypted backup of the key so reinstalling keeps it — you can
          turn that off in Settings. You can also save it as a recovery key and restore it on any phone, tablet or computer.
support.q8: What can a gateway operator see?
support.a8:
Like any VPN exit, real-time encrypted flow metadata — but no log we create,
          and never your traffic contents. Turn on multi-hop so no single server sees both who you are and
          where you're going.
support.a9:
It routes your traffic through two gateways, so no single server sees both
          your IP and your destination. It's slower — the app tells you how much — and it's off by
          default.
support.a10:
No. CumulusVPN protects you from local-network snooping, ISP logging, and
          geo-restrictions, but it is not anonymity software like Tor. We say so plainly.
support.q11: How do I upgrade to premium?
support.a11: On the web at vpn.cumulusvpn.com — with FLUX from your own wallet (cheapest) or by card, Apple Pay or Google Pay. Where the iOS or Android app offers an in-app subscription, you can subscribe there through Apple or Google instead. Your device unlocks on its own about a minute after payment confirms.
support.q12: What is FLUX and how do I get it?
support.a12:
FLUX is the cryptocurrency of the Flux network. Buy it on an exchange and hold
          it in a wallet such as Zelcore or SSP, then pay from there.
support.a13: Your entitlement is computed from the public blockchain and keyed to your public key, so every gateway flips that key to full speed within about a minute — on all servers at once, for 30 days. It unlocks whichever device holds that key — there is no account. Save your recovery key to restore it on any phone, tablet or computer; it works best on one device at a time, or on devices connected to different countries.
support.a14:
Yes. Send a multiple of the monthly amount and the extra months stack (up to
          24).
support.a15: Yes. On the web, cards, Apple Pay and Google Pay are handled by Stripe; where an app offers an in-app subscription, Apple or Google handles it. The processor holds your payment details — we never see them, and there is still no account. Paying in FLUX from your own wallet stays the cheapest option.
support.q16: The app shows "no gateways" or no countries.
support.a16:
Your device probably has no working internet, or a captive portal
          (hotel/airport Wi-Fi) is blocking the gateway probe. Reconnect and reopen the app — discovery
          retries automatically.
support.a17:
Approve the operating-system VPN-permission prompt on the first connect. If
          another VPN is already active, disconnect it first, then try again — or pick a different
          country.
support.a18:
The free tier is capped at 100 KB/s server-side. Upgrade to premium for
          full speed.
support.q19: What is the VPN permission prompt?
support.a19:
Android and iOS require your explicit consent before any app can create a VPN
          tunnel. It's the operating system asking, once — approve it to connect.
support.q20: How do I fully remove myself?
support.a20:
Disconnect, then regenerate or delete your key in the app's settings. That
          severs the pseudonymous link; gateway state is RAM-only and already clears when you
          disconnect.
support.ch_email_p: Support, plus privacy and data requests. We answer from a real inbox.
support.ch_github_p: Report a bug or request a feature — the app and gateway are open source.
support.ch_community_p: Discord / Telegram community for tips and announcements.
support.ch_social_p: Follow along on X for release notes and status.
support.q21: I paid — why is my other device still slow?
support.a21: Your Premium belongs to your key, not to one device — and each app makes its own key when it is installed, so your other device has a different one. Save the recovery key on the device you paid for (in its Settings, or on the Connect page on the web) and restore it on the other device. It works best on one device at a time, or on devices connected to different countries; two devices on the same server would keep knocking each other off. To give the other device its own Premium instead, copy its Device code from Settings → About and paste it into the box on the upgrade page.
support.q22: I sent FLUX with the wrong message, or too little. What now?
support.a22: Nothing is lost, but it will not unlock on its own. A payment only grants premium if it carries your exact <mono>CVPN1:</mono> code and covers at least one day. Email support with the transaction id and the Device code from Settings → About, and we will credit it by hand — you will be asked to prove you hold the key. Automated claiming is on the roadmap.
support.q23: Can I use Premium on several devices?
support.a23: Yes. Save your recovery key and restore it on each device — Premium belongs to the key, so it comes along. It works best on one device at a time, or on devices connected to different countries: two devices on the same server knock each other off. Or give each device its own Premium by paying for its Device code (Settings → About).
support.q24: Which DNS does CumulusVPN use, and can I change it?
support.a24: By default, Cloudflare (1.1.1.1). In the web app you can switch to Mullvad DNS, which is privacy-focused and filters nothing, Google Public DNS, which filters nothing, Quad9, which blocks known malicious sites, DNS4EU, an EU-based resolver that blocks malware and phishing, AdGuard DNS, which blocks ads and trackers, or Cloudflare for Families, which blocks malware and adult content. The mobile apps will get the same choice in version 1.3.1. Your look-ups travel inside the tunnel to our server, which sends them on encrypted (DNS over HTTPS) to the provider you picked, so the provider sees the server's address, never yours, and we keep no DNS logs.

privacy.lead: CumulusVPN is a decentralized VPN service. This policy explains, in plain language, exactly what we do and do not collect. It is short because the service is built to collect almost nothing. If a claim here is ever wrong, that is a bug we will fix — the architecture is described publicly at cumulusvpn.com and in our source code.
privacy.contact_line:
Contact for privacy questions and data requests: info@cumulusvpn.com
Abuse reports: info@cumulusvpn.com
privacy.s1_h: 1. Summary (the whole policy in one screen)
privacy.s1_li1: No account. No email. No password. No phone number. You never give us your identity.
privacy.s1_li2: No activity logs. We do not record the websites you visit, your DNS queries, your traffic contents, your bandwidth history, or connection timestamps to any persistent store.
privacy.s1_li3: Your identity is a cryptographic key, generated on your own device. We never see your private key. We only ever see a public key, which is a random-looking string with no link to you.
privacy.s1_li4: Gateways keep peer state in RAM only. When a server restarts, that state is gone. There is no traffic database to seize, subpoena, or leak.
privacy.s1_li5: Payments are optional. You can pay in FLUX cryptocurrency on a public blockchain, or by card, Apple Pay or Google Pay through Stripe, Apple or Google. We do not operate the blockchain, never handle or store your card details, and never learn your name from a payment.
privacy.s1_li6: No trackers, no advertising SDKs, no analytics that identify you. The apps contain no third-party advertising or behavioural-tracking code.
privacy.s1_li7: We are not a data business. We have no user data to sell, and we do not sell data.
privacy.s2_p1: CumulusVPN ("we", "us") is a VPN service operated by InFlux Technologies LLC, 651 N Broad St, Ste 205 #9147, Middletown, DE 19709, USA. It is built on the Flux decentralized cloud network (runonflux.io). VPN exit servers ("gateways") run as containerized apps on Flux nodes with static IP addresses, owned and operated by independent third-party node operators, not by us. We publish the service; the underlying compute is decentralized.
privacy.s2_p2:
For the purposes of the EU/UK General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), to the very limited extent
      any of the information below is "personal data", InFlux Technologies LLC is the data controller; you
      can reach us at info@cumulusvpn.com. The lawful basis we rely on is our legitimate interest (Article 6(1)(f)) in providing a
      functioning, abuse-resistant VPN, and — for payments — performance of the service you request
      (Article 6(1)(b)). Because the service is designed to be anonymous, in most cases we hold no data
      that can be linked to you at all.
privacy.s3_intro: We want to be explicit, because most VPNs bury this. CumulusVPN does not collect, log, or store any of the following:
privacy.s3_li1: Your name, email address, phone number, or any account credentials — there are no accounts.
privacy.s3_li2: Your originating IP address in any persistent log.
privacy.s3_li3: The websites, domains, or services you connect to.
privacy.s3_li4: Your DNS queries (DNS is resolved for you through the tunnel and not recorded).
privacy.s3_li5: The contents, timing, or size of your traffic, in any persistent database.
privacy.s3_li6: A bandwidth history, session history, or connection-timestamp history tied to you.
privacy.s3_li7: Device advertising identifiers (IDFA / GAID) — we do not request or use them.
privacy.s3_li8: Location data from your device (GPS, precise or coarse). The country you connect through is your choice of server, not a reading of your device location.
privacy.s3_li9: Contacts, photos, files, microphone, camera, or any device sensor.
privacy.s3_p1:
We do not use third-party advertising networks, and we do not use analytics products that build a
      profile of you (such as ad-tech SDKs). The apps ship without behavioural trackers.
privacy.s3_p2: Our websites (cumulusvpn.com and vpn.cumulusvpn.com) use Cloudflare Web Analytics, a cookieless, aggregate measurement service: it sets no cookies, stores nothing on your device, and cannot identify or profile individual visitors. It tells us page counts, not people. The apps contain no analytics of any kind.
privacy.s4_h: 4. What is technically involved (and why it isn't a profile of you)
privacy.s4_intro:
A VPN cannot function without some data passing through it in real time. Here is all of it, and why
      none of it becomes a record about you.
privacy.s4_1_p: Your device generates a WireGuard key pair locally on first launch. The private key is never sent to us or to any gateway. So that deleting and reinstalling the app — or moving to a new phone — doesn't lose it, the app keeps an encrypted backup of it: in the iPhone's Keychain on iOS, and on Android in Google's Block Store, end-to-end encrypted with your screen lock so neither Google nor we can read it. The backup is on by default and can be turned off in Settings. Only the public key is sent to a gateway so it can route your encrypted tunnel. A public key is a 32-byte random-looking value. It is not tied to your name, email, or hardware, and you can regenerate it at any time. It is a pseudonym, not an identity.
privacy.s4_2_h: 4.2 In-memory peer state on the gateway
privacy.s4_2_p: While you are connected, the gateway holds — in volatile memory (RAM) only — the minimum needed to route packets: your public key, the temporary internal tunnel IP assigned to it (e.g. 10.8.x.y), and a byte counter used to enforce your speed tier. This state is never written to disk, is not shipped to any central server, and is erased when the gateway process restarts or you disconnect. There is no historical log built from it.
privacy.s4_3_p: To carry your traffic, the gateway necessarily sees the IP address your connection arrives from, in the moment, at the network layer — this is how any internet server works. CumulusVPN does not log this address to any persistent store, and does not associate it with your browsing. When your session ends, it is not retained.
privacy.s4_4_p:
DNS look-ups are resolved on your behalf through the encrypted tunnel so your local network and ISP
      cannot see them. The gateway then sends each one on encrypted, as DNS over HTTPS, to Cloudflare's public resolver (1.1.1.1) or to the one you choose (Mullvad DNS, Google Public DNS, Quad9, DNS4EU, AdGuard DNS or Cloudflare for Families). The resolver sees only the gateway's IP address, never yours. If the encrypted connection to it fails, the gateway falls back to ordinary DNS to the same resolver, except for Mullvad DNS, which accepts only encrypted look-ups. We do not keep DNS query logs.
privacy.s4_5_h: 4.5 How your app reaches the gateways
privacy.s4_5_p: Your app discovers gateways and reads their status by calling each gateway's control API directly. Those responses are signed with the gateway's ed25519 key and verified by the app, so tampering is detected even though the control channel itself is a plain connection — the integrity guarantee comes from the signature, not from a certificate. Your actual internet traffic is separate and is end-to-end encrypted by WireGuard between your device and the gateway.
privacy.s4_6_h: 4.6 What gateway operators can and cannot see
privacy.s4_6_p: Gateways run on Flux nodes owned and operated by independent third-party node operators, not by us. Like any VPN exit, an operator observing their own server can see encrypted flow metadata in real time (that a peer is sending traffic), but not a persistent log we create, and not the tunnel contents. For users who do not want any single server to see both their IP and their destination, CumulusVPN offers an optional multi-hop mode: your traffic is routed through two gateways so that no single server sees both who you are and where you are going. Multi-hop is off by default and is described honestly in the app.
privacy.s5_h: 5. Payments (only if you upgrade to premium)
privacy.s5_p1: CumulusVPN has a free tier that requires no payment and no identifying information.
privacy.s5_li1: Where you pay. On the web at vpn.cumulusvpn.com you can pay in FLUX or by card. An app may also let you pay inside it; where an app offers an in-app subscription, Apple or Google handles it. A voucher adds free days of premium to the device that redeems it.
privacy.s5_li2: You can send FLUX from your own wallet to our published payment address, including a short memo derived from your public key so the network can credit the right key. If you pay by card or through an app store instead, that processor collects those details under its own privacy policy and we receive only a confirmation. Either way we do not collect card numbers, billing addresses, or names.
privacy.s5_li3: Blockchain transactions are public by nature. However you pay, premium is granted by a FLUX transaction to our payment address that carries your memo; if you pay by card, through an app store or with a voucher, we send that transaction for you. Anyone, including us, can see on the public ledger that a payment of a certain amount was made to our address with a given memo. That ledger is operated by the Flux blockchain, not by us. We do not link that transaction to your real-world identity, and the memo is derived one-way from your public key — it does not reveal your key or your traffic. Please understand that publishing a transaction to a public blockchain is inherently public; treat your wallet's privacy accordingly.
privacy.s5_li4: Entitlement (whether a key is premium and until when) is computed deterministically from the public blockchain and keyed only to the public key. For card and in-app payments we also store the payment code and the processor’s transaction id, so renewals can be credited to the right key; when you redeem a voucher we store which payment code redeemed it, so each payment code can redeem a given voucher only once. We store no separate customer billing record with your name in it, because we do not have your name.
privacy.s5_p3: If you subscribe through Apple’s App Store or Google Play, that transaction is processed by Apple or Google under their own privacy policies; we receive only the confirmation needed to grant premium, not your payment card data.
privacy.s6_p1:
If you email us (for support or an abuse report), we receive whatever you put in that email — for
      example your email address and the text of your message. We use it only to answer you and keep it no
      longer than needed to resolve the matter. You are not required to identify yourself to use the
      service; contacting support is voluntary.
privacy.s6_p2: Optional, opt-in crash reports: if — and only if — you explicitly enable crash reporting, a crash report containing technical diagnostic information (such as the app version, device model, OS version, and a stack trace) may be sent to help us fix bugs. This is off by default, contains no browsing activity, and can be turned off at any time.
privacy.s7_p:
The CumulusVPN website (cumulusvpn.com) is a static site used for downloads and documentation. The web
      app at vpn.cumulusvpn.com hosts the payment page and our signed server directory. Neither uses advertising
      cookies or third-party behavioural trackers. Any cookies used are strictly functional (for example
      remembering light/dark theme).
privacy.s8_p1: We do not sell, rent, or trade personal data — we have essentially none to sell.
privacy.s8_p2: Because we keep no activity logs and no user identities, we have nothing to hand over in response to a data request about a user's browsing. If we receive a legally valid law-enforcement or court request, we can only provide the information we actually hold, which does not include user identities, browsing history, DNS queries, or traffic contents, because those records do not exist. Where lawful and appropriate, we intend to publish a transparency report describing requests received.
privacy.s8_p3:
We do not transfer user profiles to advertisers, data brokers, or analytics vendors, because we do not
      build user profiles.
privacy.s9_p: CumulusVPN is a global network of gateways. When you connect, your traffic egresses from the country of the server you choose. Because we do not collect personal data into a central database, there is no cross-border transfer of a personal-data store to safeguard. The choice of exit country is yours and is made fresh each session.
privacy.s10_h: 10. Your rights (GDPR / UK GDPR / CCPA and similar)
privacy.s10_intro:
Depending on where you live, you may have rights to access, correct, delete, or port your personal
      data, to object to or restrict processing, and (in California) to know what is collected and to not be
      discriminated against for exercising these rights. Because the service is anonymous:
privacy.s10_li1: Access / portability: We generally hold no personal data linked to you to provide. If you emailed support, you can ask for a copy of that correspondence.
privacy.s10_li2: Deletion: There is nothing tied to your identity for us to delete from gateways; peer state is already ephemeral RAM-only and clears on disconnect/restart. You can delete your key on your device at any time (turn off the identity backup in Settings first, so no copy remains), which fully severs the pseudonymous link.
privacy.s10_li3: Do-not-sell / do-not-share: We do not sell or share personal data, so there is nothing to opt out of.
privacy.s10_p: To exercise any right, email info@cumulusvpn.com. We may be unable to identify you in our (nonexistent) records precisely because the service is anonymous — that is the design, not an evasion. You also have the right to lodge a complaint with your local data protection authority.
privacy.s11_p:
CumulusVPN is not directed to children under 13 (or the minimum age of digital consent in your
      country). We do not knowingly collect personal data from children. Because we collect no identifying
      data from anyone, we cannot determine a user's age; the service is intended for general audiences and
      is not marketed to children.
privacy.s12_p:
Traffic is encrypted end-to-end between your device and the gateway using the WireGuard® protocol
      (modern, audited cryptography). Your private key is never sent to us or to any gateway; outside the app, it exists only in the encrypted backup described in section 4.1, which you can turn off, and in any recovery key you choose to save, which stays under your control. Server-side peer state is
      kept in memory only. The app reaches each gateway's control API over a direct connection whose
      responses are ed25519-signed and verified by the app, so the authenticity of the server directory and
      gateway responses is protected by digital signatures rather than by a transport certificate.
privacy.s13_p: If we change this policy, we will update the "Last updated" date above and post the new version at cumulusvpn.com/privacy. Material changes will be highlighted. Because we keep no mailing list, the website is the authoritative source for the current policy.

terms.lead: These Terms of Service (the "Terms") are an agreement between you and InFlux Technologies LLC ("we", "us"), which develops CumulusVPN and sells CumulusVPN Premium. They cover the CumulusVPN apps, the web app at vpn.cumulusvpn.com, this website, and access to the VPN gateways the apps connect you to (together, the "Service"). We have kept them short and in plain language. By using the Service you agree to these Terms; if you do not agree, please do not use it. What we do and do not collect is explained in our Privacy Policy, and nothing in these Terms changes it. Section 16 contains an arbitration agreement and a class-action waiver that affect how disputes are resolved.
terms.s1_li1: The free tier is free. No account, no email, no payment details. Just a speed limit.
terms.s1_li2: Premium is paid time for one key. It belongs to that key's anonymous payment code, not to a person, an account or a particular device, and every payment becomes a transaction on the Flux blockchain that cannot be reversed.
terms.s1_li3: Your key is your identity, so look after it. There is no account to recover. If you lose your key and every backup of it, premium time paid to it cannot be restored.
terms.s1_li4: Use it lawfully. No illegal activity, no abuse, no spam, no attacks, and never anything involving the sexual abuse or exploitation of children.
terms.s1_li5: No uptime guarantee. The network is decentralized: gateways and countries come and go, and speeds vary.
terms.s1_li6: A VPN, not an invisibility cloak. CumulusVPN protects your traffic from your local network and your internet provider. It is not anonymity software like Tor.
terms.s2_h: 2. Who we are and what these Terms cover

We do not own, host or rent those machines, we have no physical or administrative access to them, and their operators are not our employees, agents or contractors. We do not operate the Flux network or its blockchain. We do run this website, the web app and the payment service that turns card payments and vouchers into premium time.

terms.s4_1_p: The free tier costs nothing and needs no account, no email and no payment details. Its speed is limited (currently to 100 KB/s) so that it can stay free and is hard to abuse. Every country and every gateway is available on the free tier.

Actual speeds depend on the gateway you use, the network in between and your own connection, and are not guaranteed.

terms.s4_4_h: 4.4 What a VPN can and cannot do
terms.s4_4_p: CumulusVPN encrypts your traffic between your device and the gateway and lets you choose the country it leaves from. That protects you from snooping on your local network, from logging by your internet provider, and from some geo-restrictions. It is not anonymity software like Tor: websites can still recognize you through logins, cookies and browser fingerprinting, a gateway operator can see encrypted flow metadata in real time (see section 4.6 of our Privacy Policy), and no VPN can protect a device that is already compromised. Some websites and services block VPN traffic, and we do not guarantee access to any particular one. Traffic leaves the gateway for the wider internet just as it would leave your own connection, so use end-to-end encryption such as HTTPS for anything sensitive.
terms.s5_h: 5. Your key and Device code (there is no account)
terms.s5_p1: CumulusVPN has no accounts. The first time you open an app or the web app, it generates a WireGuard key pair on your device. The public key, and the payment code derived from it (shown as the Device code under Settings → About in the app), are how the Service recognizes your key. Premium time belongs to that code, whichever device holds the key, including a device you restore it on with its recovery key.
terms.s5_li1: Keeping your key safe. The apps keep an encrypted backup of your key by default (see section 4.1 of our Privacy Policy). You are responsible for that backup, for any recovery key you keep, and for any device that holds your key. Anyone who has your key can use the premium time attached to it.
terms.s5_li2: Not losing it. We never see your private key, so we cannot recover, reset or reissue it. If you lose your key and every backup of it, or regenerate or delete it, premium time already paid to its code stays with that code. An active card or app-store subscription can be moved to a new device for the rest of its billing period and future renewals, within the limits shown in the apps and on the upgrade page.
terms.s5_li3: Paying for the right device. If you pay for another device, check its Device code before you pay. A mistyped code can still be valid, and a payment made to it cannot be reversed.
terms.s6_intro: You can buy premium in any of the ways below. Prices are shown before you pay. We may change prices for future purchases; a price change never affects premium time you have already paid for, and if we change the price of an existing card subscription we will tell you before the new price applies, so that you can cancel first.
terms.s6_1_p: Premium paid in FLUX costs $0.99/month. You pay from your own wallet. Before you send anything, the upgrade page at vpn.cumulusvpn.com, or an app that offers FLUX payment, shows the exact FLUX amount for a month, our payment address and the message to include. A month's amount adds 30 days of premium; you can pay for several months at once, and paid time stacks up to 24 months. A payment grants premium only if it carries your exact CVPN1: code and covers at least one day. If yours did not, email us the transaction id and your Device code and we may, at our discretion, credit it by hand once you prove you hold the key. The FLUX amount for a month may be adjusted as the FLUX exchange rate moves; an adjustment never changes what an earlier payment granted. FLUX payments are one-off: nothing renews, and there is nothing to cancel.
terms.s6_2_p: On the web you can subscribe for $1.99/month or $14.99/year by card, or by another payment method Stripe offers at checkout. Checkout is handled by Stripe, which holds your payment details under its own terms; we never see your card. Card subscriptions renew automatically at the end of each billing period until you cancel, and by subscribing you authorize us, through Stripe, to charge the price shown at the start of each new period. You can cancel, update your card or switch between monthly and yearly at any time under "Your subscription" on the upgrade page, or from the link in your Stripe receipt email. A cancellation takes effect at the end of the period you have already paid for: you keep premium until then and are not charged again. Plan switches are prorated, and the premium time we grant reflects what you actually paid.

terms.s6_3_p: Where the iOS or Android app offers a subscription, it is sold, billed and renewed by Apple or Google at the price shown in the store, under their terms. terms.s6_4_p: We sometimes issue voucher codes. A free-time code adds the stated number of days of premium to the key (payment code) that redeems it; a discount code lowers the price of a card checkout. Each key (payment code) can redeem a given code once, and codes can expire or run out. Codes have no cash value, cannot be exchanged for money and may not be sold. Days granted by a voucher are settled on-chain like any other payment and stay with the key that redeemed them.
terms.s6_5_h: 6.5 How premium is delivered, and why it cannot be undone
terms.s6_5_p: However you pay, premium is delivered the same way: as a FLUX transaction on the Flux blockchain that grants premium time to your device's anonymous payment code. When you pay in FLUX you send that transaction yourself; when you pay by card, through an app store or with a voucher, we send it for you. Every gateway reads the blockchain, so premium usually switches on within about a minute of the transaction confirming, on all gateways at once, although confirmation times are outside our control. Blockchain transactions are public and permanent: once premium time has been granted, it cannot be reversed or taken back on-chain, by you or by us.
terms.s6_6_p: Premium time is delivered as soon as your payment settles, and by paying you ask us to start providing it straight away. Because it is granted on-chain and cannot be taken back, payments are non-refundable except where the law requires otherwise; where the law gives you a right to withdraw from a purchase, you agree, to the extent the law allows, that this right ends once delivery has begun. If you think you were charged in error, email us and we will look into it. If a card payment is refunded, or you dispute it with your bank or card issuer, we may cancel the subscription it belongs to so that it does not renew. Refunds for App Store and Google Play purchases are handled by Apple and Google under their own policies.
